title: Using a Code Word to Help Others to Regulate Their Bad Behavior
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece offers a practical coaching tactic for helping self-aware colleagues catch themselves repeating a specific bad habit in real time. Rather than calling someone out verbally in the moment — which tends to embarrass and trigger defensiveness even when requested — the article recommends privately agreeing on a discreet code word or phrase that signals the behavior is happening. It compares the approach to a parenting trick used to curb children's behavior at social events, arguing it works just as well with adults because it interrupts the pattern without public confrontation. The piece is careful to note the tactic only works with prior buy-in from the person being signaled.
points: The core problem addressed is that people often can't see their own bad behavior while they're actively engaged in it.
A quietly agreed-upon code word interrupts the pattern without the embarrassment of a spoken, public correction.
The tactic mirrors a childhood parenting technique for curbing behavior at social functions, and works comparably well with adults.
Prior consent is essential — the article stresses confirming the person is genuinely open to this kind of feedback before deploying it.
quotes: The hard part is seeing their bad form while they are in action or in the throes of engaging others.

But saying so out loud can be embarrassing or off-putting. Such a spoken warning or spotlight will likely be seen as an admonishment and create defensiveness even when it has been requested by the transgressor.
The best code words are not noticed or recognized by others, but they highlight to the offender that they are repeating the mistake they have vowed not to make.
The code word asks them to pause and reflect on what they are doing. This gives them the chance to course correct and change their behavior mid-stream before real damage is done.
Before deploying this strategy, be sure to confirm with the leader or team member that they are open to this feedback in the current meeting or situation.
